PIPE=1 registers sum4, cutting the 16:1 operand mux, the 8x8 multiply and the 3-level adder tree out of the accumulate path, for 4608 datapath flops plus 2 control flops (ccnt one bit wider than kcnt, plus v_sr[0]) = 29194 total, VERIFIED against the netlist. NOTE this record was logged with --log-only because the flow succeeded but trial.sh's logging step was corrupted by editing the script while it ran.

X2-Y0: the SAME RTL as X1-Y1 (PIPE=1) at a 2.00 ns target instead of 2.80. X1's row was measurement-limited, not design-limited: its worst path ends at s4r (the register PIPE=1 created), is logically shorter than Y0's, and yet had identical WNS because the tool relaxed it -- TNS -35.958 -> -0.763, endpoints 2812 -> 41, 51786 buffer cells never inserted. This asks the flow for something it must actually work for. Reference X1-Y1: 350.4 MHz, setup -0.0539, TNS -0.763, 457390 cells, skew 0.2547. PREDICTION: fmax materially above 350 MHz, since the previous number was the target rather than the design. WATCH: TNS and violating endpoints should RISE (the tool working again), and clock skew should rise as it works the clock tree harder. If fmax does NOT move, the design really is at ~350 MHz and the wall is wire or skew, not logic depth.

X2-Y1: PIPE=2 registers prod[], splitting the 8x8 multiply from the 3-level adder tree. THE EXPENSIVE CUT -- 16,384 flops (4 x 16b x 256), two thirds of the entire tile register file, for one pipeline stage. Predicted total 45,579 flops (29,194 + 16,384 + v_sr[1]). Target 1.80 ns, derived from X2-Y0's measured need of 2.470 whose logic portion is 2.116 after subtracting skew 0.214, uncertainty 0.100 and setup 0.04; a 27% overreach, comparable to Y0's 19% which converged cleanly. Reference X2-Y0 (PIPE=1): 404.8 MHz, needs 2.470, TNS -1067.8, 492398 cells, 971277 um2, skew 0.2140, hold +0.0227. PREDICTION: the multiply still dominates the split so the gain should be smaller than PIPE=1's +54.7 MHz, and 16,384 flops will push skew up again -- X2 declared that pipelining spends skew to buy logic delay. WATCH: if fmax gain per flop has collapsed, the ladder is at its declared self-limiting point and X3 must be physical, not another pipeline stage.

X2-Y2: PIPE=3 also registers the selected operands (b_row 512b + 16 a_dw x 32b = 1024 flops), splitting the 16:1 tile mux off the front of the multiply. The CHEAPEST cut in the ladder, against PIPE=2's 16,384. Predicted 46,604 flops. DELIBERATE DEVIATION from X2's stated procedure: the target is 1.80 ns, the SAME as X2-Y1, rather than derived from Y1's measured need -- because at an identical target PIPE=2 and PIPE=3 are exactly one variable apart, which is a cleaner comparison than two variants at two targets. This is only valid if neither saturates, so the check is TNS: if Y2's TNS comes back small (like X1-Y1's -0.8) the target saturated it and the number is the target, not the design, and it must be re-run tighter. Launched in parallel with Y1 because two ORFS runs in their serial phases use 229% of 1800% CPU. PREDICTION: small gain -- the mux is short compared to the multiply -- but at 1024 flops the MHz-per-flop could still beat PIPE=2's, which is the number that decides whether the ladder continues.

goal: X2-Y3 is a CALIBRATION, not a ladder rung: the same PIPE=2 RTL as X2-Y1 at 1.50 ns instead of 1.80, to test whether the ladder's numbers are at each variant's LIMIT or merely equally STRAINED. The distinction matters because PIPE=1 improved its achieved need by 0.384 ns (2.854 -> 2.470) purely from being asked for more, and while PIPE=2 at 1.80 is demonstrably not saturated (TNS -906), not-saturated is not the same as maximally-optimised -- the tool also stops when its effort budget runs out. X2-Y1 reference: needs 2.072, 482.7 MHz, 577348 cells, TNS -906.0, hold +0.0353. PREDICTION: if 1.50 yields a need materially below 2.072 then every ladder number is effort-limited, the +77.9 MHz for PIPE=2 is a lower bound, and comparing variants at one fixed target is only valid as a relative ordering rather than as absolute fmax. If it lands at ~2.07 again, 482.7 really is PIPE=2's limit and the ladder numbers can be quoted as such.

X2-Y4: CALIBRATION of PIPE=3, the same RTL as X2-Y2 at 1.60 ns instead of 1.80. X2-Y2's 511.4 MHz was flagged in the same breath as a LOWER BOUND, because its TNS of -31.6 is an order of magnitude nearer saturation than PIPE=2's -906 while it needs only 1.955 against a 1.80 target -- the same shape as the X1 trap: not saturated by the |TNS| < 5 test, but no longer straining either. Reference X2-Y2: needs 1.955, 511.4 MHz, 514700 cells, TNS -31.6, hold +0.0329, skew 0.1911. PREDICTION: a need materially below 1.955, which would mean the headline +46.1% is understated and the campaign's numbers are all lower bounds. If it lands at ~1.955 again then 511.4 is genuinely PIPE=3's limit and the ladder can be quoted as absolute. WATCH hold: it has held at +0.03 throughout but each tightening makes the tool size cells up, which shortens min-delay paths.

goal: X4-Y0: re-baseline the X3-Y0 RTL (PIPE=3 RD_REG=1) at 1.40 ns. NO RTL CHANGE -- flops must stay 47116, which is the guard that nothing drifted. PURPOSE: find out whether the multiplier carry chain is actually binding before spending a Y on carry-save accumulation. At 1.60 ns the compute datapath MET its target with reg->reg WS +0.0818, so the carry chain has never been observed to fail and X4's blame assignment is so far unfalsified rather than confirmed. Committing to carry-save on an unmeasured limiter would repeat the X2-Y2 mistake: reasoning about a variant from a number that was not measuring it. PREDICTION 1 (the objective): reg->reg capability is 1.60-0.0818 = 1.518 ns, so at a 1.40 target expect reg->reg WS about -0.118 and regreg_fmax_mhz about 659 -- essentially UNCHANGED from X3-Y0's 658.7. If it lands near 659 the design is genuinely at its wall and carry-save is justified. If it lands well above (say >690) the path was merely effort-limited and no RTL change is warranted yet. PREDICTION 2 (a self-check on the metric fix): the output-port path's arrival is roughly fixed at 1.191 while its required time falls to 0.8*1.40-0.100 = 1.020, so setup WS should be about -0.171 and implied_fmax_mhz about 637 -- HIGHER than X3-Y0's 620.8 despite identical hardware. If that happens it is a fresh empirical confirmation of the period-scaled I/O artifact, not an improvement, and sta_limiter.sh must flag the row OUT-PORT and file the bug automatically.

goal: X4-Y1: retarget the SAME RTL (PIPE=3 RD_REG=1) to 1.20 ns. Still NO RTL change -- flops must stay 47116. X4-Y0 refuted X4's premise: at 1.40 the reg->reg path improved to 698.9 MHz (from 658.7 at 1.60) with zero RTL change, so the multiplier carry chain was EFFORT-LIMITED, not at its wall, and carry-save accumulation is not yet justified. X4-Y0's TNS was only -1.56, inside the |TNS|<5 saturation band, meaning the tool met its target and stopped -- so 698.9 is a floor, not a limit. This trial keeps tightening until the design genuinely fails, which is the only way to locate the wall. PREDICTION: if still effort-limited, reg->reg fmax lands 720-760 and TNS stays small (|TNS| < ~20). If the wall is near, TNS blows up by an order of magnitude while reg->reg fmax gains little over 698.9 -- that combination, large TNS with a stalled objective, is the signature of a real limit rather than a target, and it is the point at which carry-save becomes justified. NOTE X4-Y0 also corrected my model of the I/O artifact: the output-port arrival is NOT period-independent (1.191 at 1.60 -> 1.085 at 1.40), so the tool improves that path too and implied_fmax mixes artifact with real gain. Watch cost: X4-Y0 bought its 40 MHz for +1.9% cells but +16% POWER (2.098 -> 2.436 W), so power is the metric to watch as the target tightens, not area.
